creator: Alexander Terp
description:
docs/observations/herdr-0.8.0.md section 8 quotes `diff-corpus corpus/herdr-0.8.0 corpus/herdr-0.8.0-linux` printing "0 difference(s) across 15 shared scenario(s)". Measured 2026-09-06 it printed 7, and 6 after slot 2 added a layout-replay recording. So the doc asserts a thing that is no longer true, and it is the evidence a reader is pointed at.

What drifted:

- `sending-text` is macOS-only.
- `read-depth` gained five facts on macOS the Linux side never recorded: alternate_screen_read, blank_bottom_read, erase_scrollback_read, main_screen_history_survives_the_alternate_screen, trimmed_rows_are_the_blank_remainder_of_the_viewport.

**This is not a CI hole.** `./dev --corpus-linux` records Linux fresh into a scratch directory and diffs that, so it never reads the stale checked-in copy - the workflow that guards against a herdr re-pin moving one platform and not the other still works. What is stale is the checked-in evidence and the sentence quoting it.

Fix is `probe --remote` for the missing scenarios and re-quoting the block. The reason it matters despite not being a CI hole: docs/observations exists so a claim can be chased to a transcript, and a transcript that no longer says what the prose says is worse than no transcript.

Found by slot 2, 2026-09-06.
title: The checked-in Linux corpus has drifted, and an observation doc still claims it has not
